D.treatment: flexible drift-rate and response-boundary change model

O.outcome_detail: model fit to response-time and accuracy data

cells.quote: We first compared the most complex model ( ﬂexible DR ﬂexible RB) to the simplest model ( constant DR constant RB), ﬁnding that the model allowing ﬂexible change in parameters over time ﬁt better (ΔLOOIC = −3650.5).
cells.note: Lower LOOIC indicates better model fit.

D.treatment: continuous drift-rate and flexible response-boundary model
D.comparison: flexible drift-rate and flexible response-boundary model

O.outcome_detail: model fit and inferred evidence-accumulation dynamics

cells.quote: In contrast, a model in which DR was a continuous function of overall trial number while RB ﬂexibly changed did improve model ﬁt over the more complex ( ﬂexible DR ﬂexible RB) model ( ΔLOOIC = −301.2).
cells.note: The winning model specified continuous cumulative-trial change in drift rate and flexible change in response boundary.

cells.quote: The continuous DR ﬂexible RB parameterization was the best-ﬁtting model in 19/21 participants using LOOIC comparisons and 15/21 participants using Bayes Factor comparisons.
cells.note: The same six candidate models were fit separately to each participant.
